dl-01-c2.text: Atilim Gunes Baydin, Barak A. Pearlmutter, Alexey Andreyevich Radul, Jeffrey Mark Siskind (2018). Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey. Journal of Machine Learning Research 18(153), 1-43.
dl-01-c2.quote: Because machine learning practice principally involves the gradient of a scalar-valued objective with respect to a large number of parameters, this establishes the reverse mode, as opposed to the forward mode, as the mainstay technique
dl-01-c2.claim: Neural network training has one scalar output (the loss) and millions to billions of inputs (the parameters). Reverse-mode wins by a factor of n.

dl-01-c3.text: Razvan Pascanu, Tomas Mikolov, Yoshua Bengio (2013). On the difficulty of training Recurrent Neural Networks. Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 28(3).
dl-01-c3.quote: We propose a gradient norm clipping strategy to deal with exploding gradients and a soft constraint for the vanishing gradients problem.
dl-01-c3.claim: For exploding gradients, the standard fix is gradient clipping, which rescales the gradient vector to have norm at most some threshold

dl-02-c3.text: Shibani Santurkar, Dimitris Tsipras, Andrew Ilyas, Aleksander Madry (2018). How Does Batch Normalization Help Optimization?. arXiv (NeurIPS 2018).
dl-02-c3.quote: it makes the optimization landscape significantly smoother
dl-02-c3.claim: showed that BatchNorm's actual benefit is smoothing the loss landscape

dl-03-c2.text: Ilya Loshchilov, Frank Hutter (2017). Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization. arXiv (ICLR 2019).
dl-03-c2.quote: decoupling the weight decay from the optimization steps taken w.r.t. the loss function
dl-03-c2.claim: AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2019) decouples weight decay from the gradient update.

dl-05-c2.text: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun (2015). Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition. arXiv.
dl-05-c2.quote: On the ImageNet dataset we evaluate residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers

dl-06-c2.text: Tri Dao, Daniel Y. Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré (2022). FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness. arXiv.
dl-06-c2.quote: uses tiling to reduce the number of memory reads/writes
dl-06-c2.claim: FlashAttention tiles the computation, keeps blocks in fast on-chip SRAM, and never writes the full matrix.

dl-07-c2.text: Jordan Hoffmann, Sebastian Borgeaud, Arthur Mensch, et al (2022). Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models. arXiv.
dl-07-c2.quote: uses the same compute budget as Gopher but with 70B parameters
dl-07-c2.claim: Chinchilla (70B params, 1.4T tokens) outperformed it at equal compute.

dl-09-c2.text: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn (2023). Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model. arXiv.
dl-09-c2.quote: a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form
dl-09-c2.claim: shows that you can derive a closed-form mapping between the optimal policy and a reward function

dl-10-c1.text: Yaniv Leviathan, Matan Kalman, Yossi Matias (2022). Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding. arXiv (ICML 2023).
